## Description {#details}

This header provides a suite of type trait templates and metaprogramming utilities employed throughout the µTest++ framework.

The file defines templates for function traits, type lists, identity, value wrappers, and compile-time checks for container types, floating point types, and type convertibility. It also includes generic integral and floating point constant wrappers, as well as mechanisms for SFINAE and requirements checking.

These utilities facilitate advanced template programming, type deduction, and compile-time introspection, supporting the flexible and type-safe design of the µTest++ framework.

All definitions reside within the <code><Link to="/docs/api/namespaces/micro-os-plus/micro-test-plus/type-traits">micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::type&#95;traits</Link></code> namespace, ensuring clear separation from user code and minimising the risk of naming conflicts.

All relevant source files are organised within the <code>include/micro-os-plus</code> folder to maintain a structured and modular codebase.

This file is intended for internal use within the framework and should not be included directly by user code.

  labels = {["constexpr", "static"]}>
Variable template to determine if a type provides an <code>epsilon</code> member.

---

The <code>has&#95;epsilon&#95;v</code> variable template evaluates to <code>true</code> if the given type <code>T</code> defines a member named <code>epsilon</code>. This trait is determined at compile time using SFINAE and the <code>is&#95;valid</code> utility, and is used throughout the µTest++ framework to enable generic handling of types that represent floating-point values or require precision control.

</ParametersList>

The <code>is&#95;container&#95;v</code> variable template evaluates to <code>true</code> if the given type <code>T</code> provides both <code>begin()</code> and <code>end()</code> member functions, indicating that it models a standard container concept. This trait is determined at compile time using SFINAE and is&#95;valid, and is used throughout the µTest++ framework to enable generic handling of container types in template metaprogramming.

Variable template to determine if a type is a floating point type.

---

The <code>is&#95;floating&#95;point&#95;v</code> variable template evaluates to <code>true</code> if the given type <code>T</code> is a floating point type (<code>float</code>, <code>double</code>, or <code>long double</code>). For all other types, it evaluates to <code>false</code>. This trait is used throughout the µTest++ framework to enable type-safe handling and specialisation for floating point types in template metaprogramming.

Specialisations are provided for <code>float</code>, <code>double</code>, and <code>long double</code>, each evaluating to <code>true</code>.

<ParametersListItem name="false">otherwise.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<Link id="l00530" /><CodeLine lineNumber="530"><Highlight kind="normal">    </Highlight><Highlight kind="comment">// -&gt; decltype(bool(To(declval&lt; From &gt;())))</Highlight><Highlight kind="normal"></Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00531" /><CodeLine lineNumber="531"><Highlight kind="normal">    </Highlight><Highlight kind="comment">/&#42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00532" /><CodeLine lineNumber="532"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; @brief Function template to determine if one type is convertible to</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00533" /><CodeLine lineNumber="533"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; another.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00534" /><CodeLine lineNumber="534"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00535" /><CodeLine lineNumber="535"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; @details</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00536" /><CodeLine lineNumber="536"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; The &#96;is&#95;convertible&#96; function template checks, at compile time, whether</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00537" /><CodeLine lineNumber="537"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; a value of type &#96;From&#96; can be implicitly converted to type &#96;To&#96;. This is</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00538" /><CodeLine lineNumber="538"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; achieved using SFINAE and is primarily used as an implementation detail</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00539" /><CodeLine lineNumber="539"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; for the &#96;is&#95;convertible&#95;v&#96; variable template within the µTest++</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00540" /><CodeLine lineNumber="540"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42; framework.</Highlight></CodeLine>
<Link id="l00541" /><CodeLine lineNumber="541"><Highlight kind="comment">     &#42;</Highlight></CodeLine>
